editorial_reason: The Stacks 10.119.8 definition assumes a discrete valuation ring A before imposing a principal maximal-ideal generator requirement. The Stacks 10.50.13(3) discrete-value-group characterization supplies the restricted ambient ring concept without asserting all local rings admit a uniformizer.

A DVR is a commutative unital local domain with a unique proper maximal ideal; a uniformizer is defined by generating that maximal ideal. The independent maximal-ideal meaning supplies proper inclusion and maximality, without identifying arbitrary ring elements as uniformizers.

The defining equation (π)=m compares a principal ring ideal and the maximal ideal of a discrete valuation ring. The general two-sided ideal supplies the underlying ideal closure; principal generation and maximality are additional requirements, so this is not a generic local-ring generator assertion.
